Count the percentage over every atom of the '+' molecules, whether or not it takes part in a bond. If several elements tie for most common, report each of them.

trace.query:
-- Count atoms by element in '+' labeled molecules that take part in at least one bond
SELECT a.element, COUNT(DISTINCT a.atom_id) AS atom_count
FROM atom a
JOIN molecule m ON a.molecule_id = m.molecule_id
JOIN connected c ON a.atom_id = c.atom_id
WHERE m.label = '+'
GROUP BY a.element
ORDER BY atom_count DESC;

-- Count all atoms by element in '+' labeled molecules
SELECT a.element, COUNT(*) AS total_atoms
FROM atom a
JOIN molecule m ON a.molecule_id = m.molecule_id
WHERE m.label = '+'
GROUP BY a.element
ORDER BY total_atoms DESC;

-- Calculate the percentage of the most common element(s) among atoms in '+' molecules that take part in bonds over all atoms in '+' molecules
WITH bonded_atoms AS (
  SELECT a.element, COUNT(DISTINCT a.atom_id) AS bonded_count
  FROM atom a
  JOIN molecule m ON a.molecule_id = m.molecule_id
  JOIN connected c ON a.atom_id = c.atom_id
  WHERE m.label = '+'
  GROUP BY a.element
), total_atoms AS (
  SELECT a.element, COUNT(*) AS total_count
  FROM atom a
  JOIN molecule m ON a.molecule_id = m.molecule_id
  WHERE m.label = '+'
  GROUP BY a.element
), max_bonded AS (
  SELECT MAX(bonded_count) AS max_count FROM bonded_atoms
)
SELECT b.element, ROUND(1.0 * b.bonded_count / t.total_count * 100, 2) AS percentage
FROM bonded_atoms b
JOIN total_atoms t ON b.element = t.element
JOIN max_bonded m ON b.bonded_count = m.max_count
ORDER BY b.element;

trace.question: I'm compiling bond records of unusual carcinogenic molecules for a structural alert review. Please find the bonds that belong to carcinogenic molecules (labelled '+') that contain an element recorded for no other molecule in the dataset. Note that this search covers the whole dataset, so an element counts as belonging to no other molecule when no molecule other than the one at hand records it. For each such bond, return only the bond id and molecule id.
trace.evidence: A '+' label means carcinogenic.

trace.query:
-- Find elements that appear in exactly one molecule
WITH ElementMoleculeCount AS (
  SELECT element, molecule_id, COUNT(DISTINCT molecule_id) OVER (PARTITION BY element) AS molecule_count
  FROM atom
), UniqueElements AS (
  SELECT element, molecule_id
  FROM ElementMoleculeCount
  WHERE molecule_count = 1
), CarcinogenicMolecules AS (
  SELECT molecule_id
  FROM molecule
  WHERE label = '+'
), UniqueElementsInCarcinogens AS (
  SELECT ue.element, ue.molecule_id
  FROM UniqueElements ue
  JOIN CarcinogenicMolecules cm ON ue.molecule_id = cm.molecule_id
)
SELECT DISTINCT b.bond_id, b.molecule_id
FROM bond b
JOIN atom a ON b.molecule_id = a.molecule_id
JOIN UniqueElementsInCarcinogens ueic ON a.element = ueic.element AND a.molecule_id = ueic.molecule_id
ORDER BY b.bond_id
LIMIT 50;

trace.question: I'm building a control group of nitrogen-containing structures for a carcinogenicity review. How many molecules in the database contain at least one nitrogen atom, where none of those nitrogen atoms takes part in a double bond or a triple bond? A nitrogen held only by single bonds is fine; any nitrogen in a double or triple bond disqualifies the molecule. Molecules with no nitrogen at all don't count. I just need the single number of such molecules.
trace.evidence: Nitrogen refers to the element code 'n'; '=' denotes a double bond; '#' denotes a triple bond; '-' denotes a single bond.

trace.query:
-- Find molecules with nitrogen atoms
WITH NitrogenAtoms AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT molecule_id, atom_id
  FROM atom
  WHERE element = 'n'
),
-- Find nitrogen atoms involved in double or triple bonds
NitrogenDoubleTripleBonds AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT a.molecule_id, a.atom_id
  FROM atom a
  JOIN connected c ON a.atom_id = c.atom_id
  JOIN bond b ON c.bond_id = b.bond_id
  WHERE a.element = 'n' AND b.bond_type IN ('=', '#')
),
-- Molecules with nitrogen atoms but no nitrogen atoms in double or triple bonds
QualifiedMolecules AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT n.molecule_id
  FROM NitrogenAtoms n
  LEFT JOIN NitrogenDoubleTripleBonds ndt ON n.atom_id = ndt.atom_id
  WHERE ndt.atom_id IS NULL
)
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT molecule_id) AS qualified_molecule_count
FROM QualifiedMolecules;
